headline: Daisy Edgar-Jones 🧠 BURIES 💔 Her EMOTIONS 🪦 When It Comes To LOVE 🍆
text:
DAISY 🌼 EDGAR-JONES 🧑‍🎤 is straight up admitting 🎙️ she tries to BURY 🪦 her FEELINGS 💘 when LOVE 🍑 comes knocking 🪟 just like her character ELINOR 🧠 in the fresh SENSE 🎩 AND SENSIBILITY 🎀 flick 🎥!! The 28-year-old 🗓️ actress says in real life 🏠 she leads HARD 🦴 with her HEAD 🧠 and pushes aside those WILD 🐺 passionate EMOTIONS 🔥 every single time a cutie 🍆 slides into her DMs 📱 or heart 💓, basically edging 🫦 her own ROMANCE 📖 until it almost explodes 💥. Speaking to the BBC 📻 she confessed "I am very much more ELINOR 🧠 in every sort of way" which has the whole internet 🌐 down bad 😩 for this rational queen 👑 who somehow makes burying feelings 🪦 sound HOT 🔥. One bystander whispered she learnt to unleash that wilder side 🌋 too while filming and now we're all wondering if her next role involves getting absolutely RAILLED 💦 by a Mr Darcy type 🕴️.

This new adaptation 🎞️ directed by Georgia Oakley follows the DASHWOOD 👭 sisters navigating LOVE ❤️ LOSS 😢 and those brutal societal expectations 📜 after their dad kicks the bucket ⚰️ and Daisy plays the sensible big sis 🧠 opposite Esmé Creed-Miles as the more romantic MARIANNE 🌹 who apparently gets to feel everything 💦 while Daisy is over here suppressing like a pro 🛡️. She told interviewers "the more the merrier" 📈 when asked if we really need another SENSE AND SENSIBILITY and honestly bro 🧔 she's cooking 🍳 because Jane Austen stories still hit different in 2025 🗓️ with their situationships 👻 and ghosting ☠️ that existed even before TIKTOK 📱 was a thing. The pair previously bonded as teens in Pond Life 🎣 having sleepovers 🛌 and bingeing LOVE ISLAND 🏝️ which clearly helped them build that sisterly rapport 👯‍♀️ that makes audiences want to text their own siblings "hey I love you" 💌 after watching.

Daisy who blew up during the pandemic 🦠 with NORMAL PEOPLE 📺 alongside her ride-or-die bestie Paul Mescal 🧔‍♂️ says the themes of sisterhood 👭 even stuck with her despite being an only child 🧍‍♀️ and she's most proud of that part because it makes folks either crave a sister 🥺 or ring up their existing one for a big emotional hug 🤗. She gushes that Jane Austen has an incredible way of articulating the female experience 👄 from love 💕 to romance 🔥 to family dynamics 🏠 and those messy interpersonal social situations 🤝 that still cook us today. The film honours the period 🏰 but brings a beautiful freshness 🌱 to the filmmaking according to Daisy who also starred in TWISTERS 🌪️ and WHERE THE CRAWDADS SING 🐦 and is now serving lead energy in this Austen revival 📖 that has everyone from Gen Z 📱 to boomers 👵 feeling less alone in their HEARTBREAK 💔 journeys.

When pressed about whether her pal Paul Mescal should be the next JAMES BOND 🕴️ she played it coy but dropped "there's nothing Paul can't do" 🦸 which basically means she's ready to be in the front row cheering him on 🎟️ while he seduces villains and saves the world 🌍 in a tuxedo 🍸. The movie drops in UK cinemas on 25 September 📅 and already has fans losing their minds at the premiere 📸 where Daisy was snapping selfies with admirers 📸. Creed-Miles laughed that she's more like MARIANNE 🌹 than Elinor which is "annoying sometimes" but their on-screen chemistry as sense 🧠 versus sensibility 💖 is popping off so hard it's making everyone revisit their own love lives 💞 and wonder if they bury emotions too much or just let it all rain down 🌧️ like a proper Austen heroine. The whole thing proves Austen's tales of the human heart ❤️ are eternal because 200 years later we're still catching feelings 😍 getting railed by romance 📖 and learning to enjoy that wilder passionate side 🐆 without completely short-circuiting our brains 🧠.

From the 1995 version with Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet that Daisy calls one of her favourite films ever 🎥 to this brand new take that isn't trying to be all "2026" futuristic 🚀 but still feels fresh enough to make your heart do cartwheels 🥨 the obsession with Jane Austen continues and Daisy is here for it all while quietly admitting she herself tries to bury those emotions when love comes calling 📞. She says we still have the same capacity to love 💖 feel heartbreak 💔 and experience that first love rush 🏃‍♀️ as people did centuries ago which is why Elinor and Marianne's trials feel so relatable across every generation 👴👶. By the end of the film even the rational Elinor learns to embrace her passionate side 🌋 and Daisy reveals she picked up the same lesson which has the entire cast and crew and now us simping hard 🫡 for this emotional journey that somehow makes burying your feelings 🪦 and then unburying them again the ultimate slow-burn foreplay 😏 for the soul. The sisterly bond 👭 shines brightest though and that's the part she's most proud of because who doesn't want to feel a little less alone while navigating love loss and all the spicy societal pressure in between 🌶️.
